observations.contract: Required player components and local authority
observations.trace: Player declares CharacterId, dimensions, limbs, skills, attributes, stats and SkeletonState as required components; the client plugin separately requires visibility. The player-added hook uses CharacterId to choose local control, while the server ingress derives the attacker from its client entity and independently reads weapon timing before emitting a melee intent. Typed melee and ranged requests retain distinct phases.
observations.remaining: Required components narrow the earlier simplistic missing-component suspicion; component value/timing, alternate producers, event mapping and complete server validation are not established. Client prediction and diagnostics are not authority over tactical position, damage or health.

observations.contract: Ranged windup queried before attack branch
observations.trace: AttackWeaponFacts observes the ranged windup result, and try_start_attack propagates it before choosing ranged or melee. The inspected TacticalPlayerView delegates PlayerEquipment to InventoryView; that implementation does not override weapon_ranged_windup_secs, whose trait default admits 0.3 seconds. AnimationElapsed::from_seconds accepts finite nonnegative values, including that default.
observations.remaining: This rules out the simple claim that the currently inspected melee view necessarily fails because ranged timing is absent. Other fallible melee recovery/preparation computations, alternate views, generated delegation behavior, entire server policy and native execution remain separate.

observations.trace: The client chooses reachable visible hitboxes grouped by target body, derives melee arrival with a typed acquisition timing, creates typed animation sample start/contact/end and native contact timers, and sends a MeleeActionRequest only after predicted admission. The server request handler derives attacker identity from the client and obtains authored preparation before emitting an intent; the remaining server start/contact logic is not covered by that entry alone.
observations.remaining: Actual collision filters, local versus server clock origins, sampling, buffered-attack invalidation, server phase checks and all target/consumer aliases need further independent source work. Fixture assertions were not run.

observations.contract: Previously recorded lunge-only trace trigger question
observations.trace: QuickstepTraceObservation stores the action and active/start-tick actuator state. has_changed_since compares only whether action is Dodge, actuator activity and actuator start tick. The trace computes melee_lunge.quickstep only after the unchanged-observation early return. If only that lunge flag changes while those compared fields stay equal, a changed discrepancy classification is not logged by that call.
observations.remaining: This is the same conditional historical L12 question in batch455 and queue1289, re-assessed at 95e; no additional historical unique finding. The normal install creates the quickstep movement and active push together; the motor cancels both on lunge arrival. Actual lunge-only observations, replication ordering and desired diagnostic event policy remain unproven.

observations.trace: The shared motor permits bounded recovery when a quickstep action has ended, its sample span is within the action span plus two samples, and forward velocity magnitude exceeds 0.02. During that branch it cancels the active push only if post-update forward velocity is at most 0.02; the server snapshot copies the push and optional lunge. The client trace nevertheless compares only Dodge or quickstep lunge against active push and labels inequality an animation/actuator discrepancy.
observations.remaining: A warning follows only if the client actually observes a retained active push with neither Dodge nor quickstep lunge after a tracked observation change. Snapshot/animation sequencing, ordinary occurrence and intended diagnostic policy are not executed or established; no gameplay force, fatigue or movement defect is claimed.
